facts.statement: The genus Ziapelta was named in 2014 by a research team led by Victoria Arbour.
facts.quote: It was named in 2014, in a research paper led by ankylosaur researcher Victoria Arbour.

facts.statement: Fossils of Ziapelta were discovered in 2011 by an expedition led by Robert Michael Sullivan.
facts.quote: An expedition from the New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science and the State Museum of Pennsylvania, led by Robert Michael Sullivan, discovered a number of Z. sanjuanensis fossils in the Kirtland Formation in 2011.

facts.statement: Ziapelta lived during the Upper Cretaceous (Campanian) period in New Mexico.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in the Hunter Wash and De-na-zin members of the Kirtland Formation of Upper Cretaceous (Campanian) New Mexico.

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Ziapelta dates to between 72.98 and 72.62 million years ago.
facts.quote: By argon dating of ash layers the age of the holotype skull has been determined at between 72.98 and 72.62 million years old, the late Campanian.

facts.statement: Ziapelta is classified as an extinct genus of ankylosaurid dinosaur.
facts.quote: Ziapelta is an extinct genus of ankylosaurid.

facts.statement: There is only one known species in the genus Ziapelta, named Ziapelta sanjuanensis.
facts.quote: There is a single species in the genus, Ziapelta sanjuanensis.

facts.statement: The genus name Ziapelta combines the Zia sun symbol and the Latin word 'pelta' (shield), referencing the animal's armor.
facts.quote: The genus is named after the Zia sun symbol, a stylized sun with four groups of rays, having religious significance to the Zia people of New Mexico, and the iconic symbol on the state flag of New Mexico, and pelta (Latin), a small shield, in reference to the osteoderms found on all ankylosaurids.

facts.statement: The species name 'sanjuanensis' refers to San Juan County, the location of the fossil discovery.
facts.quote: The specific name (sanjuanensis) comes from San Juan County, where the fossils were discovered.

facts.statement: Most known fossils of Ziapelta consist of the front part of the animal.
facts.quote: Multiple specimens have been described to date, though the fossils are mostly from the front part of the animal.

facts.statement: The preservation of Ziapelta fossils suggests its head and neck armor may have detached from the body before burial.
facts.quote: Ziapelta is known from a complete skull and specimens of first cervical half ring, so its head and cervical armor may have been separated from the body before the specimen was buried.

facts.statement: Ziapelta sanjuanensis possesses three unique derived traits that distinguish it from other dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Ziapelta sanjuanensis showed three unique derived traits or autapomorphies.

facts.statement: Ziapelta had a large, prominent, triangular bone plate in the middle of its snout.
facts.quote: The caputegulum (middle bone plate), of the snout was large, prominent and roughly triangular in shape.

facts.statement: Ziapelta featured deep squamosal horns on its skull that measured 10.2 cm from base to tip.
facts.quote: Ziapelta had deep, anteriorly curved squamosal horns (measuring 10.2 cm from the base to the tip).

facts.statement: The rear base of the Ziapelta skull contained three deep grooves.
facts.quote: The rear base of the skull featured three deep grooves.

facts.statement: The top of the Ziapelta skull displays a mixture of concave, flat, and convex bone plates.
facts.quote: A further possible distinguishing trait is the mixture of concave, flat and convex caputegulae on the skull top.

facts.statement: The widest part of the Ziapelta skull is formed by the squamosal horns at the top rear corners, with no constriction in front of the eyes.
facts.quote: The skull has no constriction in front of the eye sockets and its widest point is formed by the squamosal horns on the top rear corners.

facts.statement: The upper jaws of Ziapelta were 11.9 cm long and held approximately eighteen small teeth on each side.
facts.quote: The maxillae, the upper jaws, were 11.9 cm long and contained about eighteen small teeth on each side.

facts.statement: The horns at the back corners of the Ziapelta skull were very high, thick, and curved forward.
facts.quote: The squamosal horns on the back corners of the skull were very high, thick and forward-curving.

facts.statement: Ziapelta's body was protected by osteoderms, which are bone scutes embedded in the skin.
facts.quote: The body of Ziapelta was protected by osteoderms, scutes of bone that sit inside of the skin.

facts.statement: Ziapelta had two cervical half-rings protecting its neck and rows of oval scutes likely running along its back and sides.
facts.quote: Apart from the osteoderms that are part of the skull, two cervical halfrings were present to protect the upper side of the neck and rows of oval scutes probably ran along the back and sides of the torso; the latter are only known as detached specimens.

facts.statement: Ziapelta's osteoderms ranged from 146 to 169 mm in length and 58 to 104 mm in width, with keels up to 10.9 cm tall.
facts.quote: The osteoderms were between 146 and 169 millimetres long, between 58 and 104 millimetres wide and their keels varied between 2.4 cm and 10.9 cm tall.

facts.statement: The closest relative of Ziapelta is debated, with Scolosaurus or Nodocephalosaurus proposed depending on the cladistic model used.
facts.quote: Its closest relative appears to be either Scolosaurus or Nodocephalosaurus, depending on what cladistic model is used.

facts.statement: The genus Ziapelta was named by Arbour and colleagues in 2014.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Arbour et al., 2014

facts.statement: The species Ziapelta sanjuanensis was described by Arbour, Burns, Sullivan, Lucas, and Cantrell in 2014.
facts.quote: species_authority: Arbour, Burns, Sullivan, Lucas, & Cantrell, 2014

facts.statement: Ziapelta lived in North America between 74.5 and 72.5 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, entre 74,5 a 72,5 millones de años durante el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica

facts.statement: Individuals of Ziapelta measured between 4.6 and 6.1 meters in length.
facts.quote: los individuos medían entre 4,6 y 6,1 metros de largo

facts.statement: Ziapelta was a quadruped with a wide and robust body.
facts.quote: Era cuadrúpedo, de cuerpo ancho y robusto

facts.statement: The front of Ziapelta's jaws was covered by a beak, followed by rows of small leaf-shaped teeth further back.
facts.quote: La parte delantera de las mandíbulas estaba cubierta por un pico, con hileras de pequeños dientes en forma de hoja más atrás

facts.statement: Researchers believe Ziapelta likely had a large club at the end of its tail, although this club has not been fossilized.
facts.quote: Se cree que Ziapelta podría haber tenido un gran garrote al final de la cola, aunque este garrote no se ha encontrado fosilizado

facts.statement: Ziapelta sanjuanensis displays three unique derived characteristics or autapomorphies.
facts.quote: Z. sanjuanensis muestra tres características únicas derivadas o autapomorfias

facts.statement: The central bony plate of the snout, called a caputegula, was large, prominent, and approximately triangular in shape.
facts.quote: La placa ósea media del hocico, denominada caputegula, era grande, prominente y de forma aproximadamente triangular

facts.statement: Ziapelta possessed high frill horns that curved forward, measuring 10.2 centimeters from base to tip.
facts.quote: Ziapelta tenía cuernos escamosales altos y curvados anteriormente, que medían 10,2 centímetros desde la base a la punta

facts.statement: The skull bones and other body parts were fused, increasing their strength.
facts.quote: Los huesos del cráneo y otras partes del cuerpo se fusionaron, aumentando así su fuerza

facts.statement: The skull of Ziapelta had a length of about 44 centimeters.
facts.quote: El cráneo tiene una longitud de unos 44 centímetros

facts.statement: The upper jaws measured 11.9 centimeters in length and contained about eighteen small teeth on each side.
facts.quote: Los maxilares , las mandíbulas superiores, medían 11,9 centímetros de largo y contenían unos dieciocho dientes pequeños a cada lado

facts.statement: The frill horns at the rear corners of the skull were very high, thick, and curved forward.
facts.quote: Los cuernos escamosos en las esquinas posteriores del cráneo eran muy altos, gruesos y curvados hacia adelante

facts.statement: Ziapelta is classified in the family Ankylosauridae and is considered a sister species to Scolosaurus from Canada in several evolutionary trees.
facts.quote: Ziapelta was placed in the Ankylosauridae, as possibly closely related to Scolosaurus from Canada, being its sister species in several of the evolutionary trees rendered by the cladistic analysis that was part of the describing paper

facts.statement: An alternative hypothesis suggests Ziapelta and Nodocephalosaurus could be sister species, though this requires only one additional shared trait and is slightly less likely.
facts.quote: However, the authors indicated that an alternative tree in which Ziapelta and Nodocephalosaurus were forced to be sister species was just one evolutionary step longer, i.e. requiring the presence of but a single additional shared trait, and thus only slightly less likely

facts.statement: Researchers propose that ankylosaurids recolonized North America from Asia during the Campanian or Turonian ages, leading to the diversification of genera including Ziapelta.
facts.quote: They propose that ankylosaurids subsequently recolonized North America from Asia during the Campanian or Turonian ages of the Late Cretaceous, and there diversified once more, leading to genera such as Euoplocephalus, Scolosaurus and Ziapelta

facts.statement: The absence of Ziapelta in habitats shared by relatives like Euoplocephalus and Scolosaurus does not prove faunal separation, as Ziapelta comes from younger geological layers.
facts.quote: Provincialism in the sense of a faunal separation between the northern and southern regions of Laramidia cannot be deduced from the fact that Ziapelta was not present in the habitat shared by its relatives Euoplocephalus, Dyoplosaurus, and Scolosaurus because Ziapelta stems from younger layers than these animals

facts.statement: Ziapelta had a body protected by osteoderms, which are bone shields embedded in the skin.
facts.quote: El cuerpo de Ziapelta estaba protegido por osteodermos, escudos de hueso que se asientan dentro de la piel.

facts.statement: The cervical osteoderms of Ziapelta were 146 to 169 mm long, 58 to 104 mm wide, and their ridges were 2.4 to 10.9 cm high.
facts.quote: Los osteodermos tenían entre 146 y 169 milímetros de largo, entre 58 y 104 milímetros de ancho y sus quillas variaban entre 2,4 centímetros y 10,9 centímetros de alto.

facts.statement: All found osteoderms of Ziapelta have a densely pitted surface but lack veins.
facts.quote: Todos los osteodermos encontrados tienen una superficie que está densamente picada pero carece de venas.

facts.statement: Some disconnected osteoderms were found, one possibly from a middle ring and another originating from the upper pectoral region.
facts.quote: Uno de estos podría haber sido originalmente parte de un medio anillo. Se vio que un segundo se originaba en la región pectoral superior del seno.

facts.statement: A 2011 expedition led by Robert Michael Sullivan discovered Ziapelta fossils in the Kirtland Formation.
facts.quote: Una expedición del Museo de Historia Natural y Ciencia de Nuevo México y el Museo Estatal de Pensilvania, liderada por Robert Michael Sullivan, descubrió una serie de fósiles de Z. sanjuanensis en la formación Kirtland en 2011.

facts.statement: The specimens were found in the Hunter Wash and De-na-zin members of the formation within the Bisti/De-Na-Zin Reserve in New Mexico.
facts.quote: Los especímenes fueron hallados en los Miembros Hunter Wash y De-na-zin de la formación en la reserva Bisti/De-Na-Zin en Nuevo México.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen NMMNH P-64484 consists of a complete skull lacking jaws, parts of the first two cervical rings, and a series of partial osteoderms.
facts.quote: Z. sanjuanensis fue identificado como una nueva especie a partir de algunos fósiles incluyendo al espécimen holotipo NMMNH P-64484 hallado en el Miembro De-na-zin y consiste en un cráneo completo carente de las mandíbulas, partes de los dos primeros anillos cervicales, y una serie de osteodermos parciales

facts.statement: The species Ziapelta sanjuanensis was named in 2014 by Victoria Arbour, Michael Burns, Robert Sullivan, Spencer Lucas, Amanda Cantrell, Joshua Fry, and Thomas Suazo.
facts.quote: En 2014 Victoria Arbour, Michael Burns, Robert Sullivan, Spencer Lucas, Amanda Cantrell, Joshua Fry y Thomas Suazo nombraron a la especie tipo Ziapelta sanjuanensis.

facts.statement: Argon dating of ash layers determined the holotype skull's age to be between 72.98 and 72.62 million years old, during the late Campanian.
facts.quote: Mediante la datación con argón de las capas de ceniza, la edad del cráneo holotipo se ha determinado entre 72,98 y 72,62 millones de años, durante el Campaniense tardío.

facts.statement: Ziapelta was placed in the family Ankylosauridae as a possible close relative of the Canadian Scolosaurus, being its sister species in several cladistic trees.
facts.quote: Ziapelta fue situado en la familia Ankylosauridae, como un posible pariente cercano de Scolosaurus de Canadá, siendo su especie hermana en varios de los árboles evolutivos presentados por el análisis cladístico que formaba parte del documento descriptivo.

facts.statement: Ziapelta and other Late Cretaceous North American ankylosaurs are grouped with Asian genera in a tribe named Ankylosaurini.
facts.quote: Dado que Ziapelta y otros anquilosáuridos norteamericanos del Cretácico superior se agrupan con géneros asiáticos, en una tribu que los autores denominaron Ankylosaurini

facts.statement: The genus Ziapelta lived from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Ziapelta is the tribe Ankylosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ankylosaurini

facts.statement: Ziapelta belongs to the family Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Ankylosauridae

facts.statement: Ziapelta is classified within the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia
